accuracy.evidence: Every rhyme pair was said aloud and checked by ending sound from the vowel on: star/are and star/car (/ɑː/), dock/clock (/ɒk/), two/shoe (/uː/), moon/spoon (/uːn/), wall/fall (/ɔːl/), spout/out (/aʊt/), wool/full (/ʊl/), hill/Jill (/ɪl/); the non-rhymes differ at the end: moon/milk, bed/bell (/d/ vs /l/), cat/dog, dock/dog, two/toes, moon/mouse. Song words match the traditional UK versions of Twinkle, Hickory Dickory Dock, One Two Buckle My Shoe, Hey Diddle Diddle, Humpty Dumpty, Incy Wincy and Baa Baa Black Sheep. The age placement follows Development Matters (birth to three: enjoy singing, sing songs and say rhymes) with spotting and suggesting rhymes left to 3-4, as the adult text says. Parameterised answers 2*n, n+k and 2*n hold at every corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early-rhyme slips: choosing by meaning not sound (cheese, coat and cup in the gap scene with the 'could fit the song, but' message; m2, m8, challenge 'meaning'), same onset taken as rhyme (dog for dock, toes for two, mouse for moon, the moon/milk pair; p3, challenge 'start'), close-but-different endings (bed/bell pair, m4, challenge 'close'), looking for rhyme at the start of a line (Find scene feedback for first words, p5, challenge 'place') and joining in on every word (frog scene clap refusals, m6, challenge 'every').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagsongrhyme is built around singing: a frog hops word by word through Twinkle, twinkle and only accepts a clap on star and are, a paused song line waits for the picture that completes the rhyme, word pairs are judged by ear, and real nursery-rhyme lines are tapped to find where the rhyme sits. Lesson 725 (flagrhyme) generates and sorts rhymes and 490 (flagbyheart) memorises songs line by line; neither has the pause-and-join-in or hop-and-clap mechanics, which are the target behaviour for 2 to 3 year olds.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers the rule by acting: hopping past star is refused with 'star is a rhyming word, clap on it', clapping on twinkle is refused with 'clap at the end of the line', dropping the dog into 'the mouse ran up the' says it starts like dock but the end sounds different, and tapping Humpty in the Find scene says it is at the start of the line. The done messages state 'same at the end' only after the scene has shown it.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with a tempting wrong option that the lab disproves: 'On every word' for when to clap (the frog refuses claps on non-rhymes), 'dog, because it starts like dock' (the gap scene rejects dog), 'Yes, they both start with m' for moon and milk (the pair scene answers Not the same), and 'At the start of a line' (every rhyme in the Find scene sits at the end).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions; wrong options carry five tagged messages naming the slip: meaning ('fits the story, but does not sound the same at the end'), start ('those words start the same; a rhyme sounds the same at the END'), close ('close is not the same; bed and bell end in different sounds'), place ('rhyming words come at the end of each line') and every ('not every word rhymes').

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs score well under the family kid limit (FK -1.8) with two-to-six-word sentences and familiar song words; canvas text is one banner line plus single words and big pictures; adult text is FK 7.3, under the family adult limit of 10, with EYFS and Letters and Sounds terms kept there.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: what a rhyme is (star, are), where it comes and how to join in, start-same is not rhyme, three spoken pairs. Adult paragraphs: EYFS and Phase 1 placement, the from-the-vowel definition and why the pause works, four named mistakes plus the no-odd-one-out caution, and what each lab scene does. The content gate's filler and 12% duplicate checks pass.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px screenshots in light and dark: frog stones wrap into two rows with 30 px tall word cards and two 170 px Hop and Clap pads, the gap scene has three 100 px picture tiles under a 160 px drop box, the pair scene shows two large picture cards over 64 px pads, Find chips wrap without clipping, and song-box card names shrink to fit their cards. The iPhone 13 walkthrough completes every Show me.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Hop and Clap, a Fill the gap with button per picture, Same and Not the same, a Line N: word button per song word, and a button per song card. The canvas aria-label reports each refusal and success in words; axe WCAG 2.1 AA ran clean in light and dark themes on desktop and iPhone 13.

sources: DfE (2021) Development Matters: Communication and Language, birth to three (enjoy singing, music and toys that make sounds; sing songs and say rhymes independently) and Literacy 3 and 4 year olds (spot and suggest rhymes)
DfES (2007) Letters and Sounds, Phase One, Aspect 5: Rhythm and rhyme
Traditional nursery rhyme texts as collected in The Oxford Dictionary of Nursery Rhymes (Opie and Opie)
